This is a 1,4-dihydropyridine with a ring NH. Reading the substituents around the ring:

- C2 carries CH3.
- C3 carries the isopropyl ester, C(=O)OC(C)C.
- C4 carries the 3-nitrophenyl group.
- C5 carries the ester C(=O)O–azetidin-3-yl, where the azetidine nitrogen bears a benzhydryl group (CH(Ph)2).
- C6 carries NH2.

The ring is N1H–C2(CH3)=C3–C4H(Ar)–C5=C6(NH2)–N1. I read the double bonds as C2=C3 and C5=C6, which matches the drawing.

The 3-nitrophenyl is attached at the ring carbon with the nitro group meta to it. The nitro group is drawn charge-separated, as [N+](=O)[O-]. No wedges or hashes are shown, so I included no stereochemistry.

SMILES assembled in pieces:
- Ring: N1C(N)=C(C(=O)OC2CN(C2)C(c3ccccc3)c3ccccc3)C(c3cccc([N+](=O)[O-])c3)C(C(=O)OC(C)C)=C1C
- Check: N1, then C(N)= is C6 with NH2, then C5 with the ester to the azetidine, then C4 with the aryl, then C3 with the isopropyl ester, =C1C is C2 with CH3. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: CC(C)OC(=O)C1=C(C)NC(N)=C(C(=O)OC2CN(C2)C(c3ccccc3)c3ccccc3)C1c1cccc([N+](=O)[O-])c1
